chunking_strategy.reasoning: The corpus is static Markdown and PDF documents with medium-length pages and factual lookup queries. Fixed-size chunking is well-suited here — the documents have consistent structure and the queries are short and direct, so semantic chunking adds complexity without meaningful quality improvement.
alternatives: Sentence-window chunking — better context preservation, slight overhead
Semantic chunking — overkill for this volume and query type
chunking_strategy.config_notes: Use 512-token chunks with 50-token overlap. Process PDFs with PyMuPDF. Strip headers/footers before chunking.

embedding_model.reasoning: Single-language English corpus, startup budget, AWS infrastructure. text-embedding-3-small gives strong retrieval quality at the lowest cost per token, and integrates natively with LlamaIndex. No need for multilingual or domain-specific models.
alternatives: text-embedding-3-large — higher quality, 5x cost, unnecessary at this scale
BAAI/bge-small-en — free, self-hosted, slightly lower quality
embedding_model.config_notes: Dimension: 1536. Batch embed on ingest. Cache embeddings to avoid re-embedding unchanged docs.

vector_database.reasoning: Static data, under 100k documents, no compliance constraints, AWS-hosted team, startup budget. Pinecone Starter tier handles this volume with zero infrastructure overhead and near-zero ops cost — the right choice for a team without ML ops experience.
alternatives: Weaviate Cloud — more features, higher cost, unnecessary here
ChromaDB (local) — free for dev, not production-grade at scale
vector_database.config_notes: Use Pinecone Starter (free tier covers 100k vectors). Create a single index with cosine similarity. Tag each vector with document_id and source metadata for filtered retrieval.

retrieval_method.reasoning: No structured data or tables in the corpus, query types are factual lookups from prose documents. Dense retrieval with good embeddings is sufficient. Hybrid BM25+dense adds operational overhead that isn't justified here.
alternatives: Hybrid BM25 + dense — better keyword matching, only needed when corpus has structured content
Sparse-only BM25 — faster, worse semantic recall
retrieval_method.config_notes: Top-k=5 for retrieval. Apply metadata filters on source type if needed. No reranker required at this QPS and complexity level.

llm_for_generation.reasoning: Internal KB Q&A requires accurate, grounded responses — not creative ones. Claude Haiku 3.5 offers strong instruction-following and citation quality at low cost, fitting a startup budget. For 10 QPS, latency is well within acceptable bounds.
alternatives: claude-sonnet-4-6 — higher quality, 5x cost, justified only for complex reasoning tasks
llm_for_generation.config_notes: System prompt: instruct model to answer only from retrieved context and cite sources. Set temperature=0 for factual consistency. Max output tokens: 512.

eval_approach.eval_dataset_guidance: Create 50–100 Q&A pairs from the existing documentation by hand or with Claude. Include at least 10 questions where the answer is NOT in the docs (to test hallucination resistance). Run RAGAS after each major corpus update.

architecture_summary: This is a straightforward semantic search RAG pipeline suited to a static internal knowledge base. Documents are chunked at fixed size, embedded with text-embedding-3-small, and stored in Pinecone. At query time, the top 5 chunks are retrieved via dense search and passed to Claude Haiku for grounded answer generation. The stack is fully managed, requiring no ML ops expertise, and can be built and deployed in 1–2 weeks with a basic engineering team.
critical_risks: Poor retrieval quality from inconsistently formatted documents — invest in a cleaning and normalisation step before chunking
Knowledge staleness — even 'static' corpora drift; build a re-ingestion trigger when docs are updated
Hallucination on out-of-scope questions — enforce strict grounding instructions in the system prompt and monitor for cases where the model answers without retrieved context
quick_wins: Stand up Pinecone index and ingest a sample of 50 documents to validate embedding quality before full ingest
Build a simple Streamlit or Slack-bot interface so employees can start using the tool within the first week
Run RAGAS on 20 hand-crafted Q&A pairs to establish a quality baseline before optimising
